title: Partitioning {1,...,n} into parts of size at most three whose sums are powers of three: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
description:
Proof of Conjecture 1 of Gurvich and Naumova (arXiv:2508.00946): for every n ≥ 1 the set {1,...,n} has a partition into parts of at most three elements whose sums are powers of 3. The partition is given by an explicit recursion; as a corollary, every {1,...,n} has a partition into parts of at most m elements with sums powers of m if and only if m is 2 or 3.

paper/ holds the LaTeX source in the Elsevier elsarticle template and the compiled PDF; dist/ holds the PDF, the arXiv tarball and MasterGurvichNaumovaZip.zip with every file of the repository. lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem (7 files); GN.gurvich_naumova states the existence of a Finpartition of Finset.Icc 1 n with the required parts and depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. checks/ contains independent implementations of the construction in Python, Julia, C and C++, and run_all.sh runs the Lean build, the axiom check and all programs.
